txt: The Precinct surgeon, chewing on a piece of candy, throws her a questioning glance, walking by: "Need a hand with that?"
The surgeon watches her for a moment, pulling on his cigarette. "You know, it's not so cold that you're going to get frostbite without your gloves."
You hear a man clearing his throat briskly, then an answer: "Gottlieb. What'd ya want?"
"*Who* you are? You lost your human visage a while back. Now let's get on with it -- I've got more important things to do."
"...do exactly that. Put yourself out of your misery. Take a deep diaphragmatic breath in and..." You hear an exaggerated inhale and a long exhale on the other end of the line.
"...or, actually!" He seems to be positively surprised by the idea. "It could be *both*, given your profile."
"Ah, it's you. Walking, talking, though?"
"And no, I *don't* want to hear a *political commentary* on the topic. In fact -- I've got work to do. Some idiot has glued his eyelids shut with Cyanoacrylate. It looks like Mack Torson."
"And you survived it! Congratulations. Are you mobile?"
"Basking in your glory, yeah. Practically drowning in it. Please, tell me what your complaint is before I am completely submerged."
"Cut down on the drinking, pal. In fact, cut *off* the drinking. The drugs too. Anything else?"
"Didn't. But now I do. How's the drinking going?"
"Do that. I need to go. Some idiot has glued his eyelids shut with Cyanoacrylate. It *looks* like Mack Torson, but it's hard to say because his eyes are swollen..."
"Even better! Anything else? I wouldn't worry about that. Officers your age have coronary trouble all the time. Also -- death is a natural part of life."
"Firewalker? Yes, yes you are. Just don't breathe in the general direction of your fire-feet. Actually, wait..."
"For you it probably is. I'm counting on my lungs outliving your liver by a wide margin." He pauses. "Not that that's anything to fête."
"From what I can tell, you're just playing into their hands -- disabling yourself from doing any actually useful work. Now, do you have any *current, pressing* medical problems?"
"Good. It would be an awful nuisance if your experiments with your blood pressure were to cause permanent damage to your vision. A nuisance to you, that is."
"Gottlieb. What is it now?" There's not the slightest hint of wanting to know the answer in that familiar raspy voice.
"Gottlieb. What'd you get yourself into this time?" The question is followed by the sound of someone taking a long drag.
"Great to hear it. Stop by some time when you're done with your case -- I'll draw some blood, run it through -- let you know how much 'forever' your liver's going to give you."
"Great! Any other complaints?"
"Great! How's the drinking going?"
"Great. Have a medal. I have an autopsy to attend to. An autopsy of one Chester McLaine, who died of *fish poisoning*."
"Great. I have an autopsy to attend to. An autopsy of one Chester McLaine, who died of *fish poisoning*."
"Hard to tell exactly what it was over the phone. Could be a combination of peripheral neuralgia and high blood pressure. Could be that you were having a heart attack..."
"I see third-degree burns and a referral to a plastic surgeon whom you won't be able to afford. But that's in the future. Do you have any *current, pressing* medical problems?"
"I'm the most serious person at this station, detective. Now, do you have any *current, pressing* medical problems?"
"Look, pal -- getting *pumped and dumped* is not a disease. People live through it all the time. You should be happy for her."
"Mhphm." The phone clicks. Suddenly you hear the already familiar voice...
"Oh, it's you. I know a woman skilled at that sort of thing over in Jamrock... but I wouldn't want to inflict you upon her. Best of luck, detective."
"Oh, spare me the sad drunken blubbering and get on with it. What's your complaint?"
"Oh," the man is unpleasantly surprised. "It's you."
"Please wonder on your own time. Now, do you have any *current, pressing* medical problems?"
"Sounds more like a newspaper headline that will surprise absolutely no one. Now, do you have any *current, pressing* medical problems?"
"That's because you're hungover -- even the radio waves coming from your direction smell like liquor." He pauses. "Do you feel like your eyes are twitching too?"
"That's the tiny vessels pulsating from high blood pressure, stupid officer. You might be sustaining permanent damage to your vision as we speak. Not much I can do about it. I'm not an *eye* doctor."
"That's what the guys say, officer. That some chick pumped you -- and then dumped you. Threw you away like an empty juice carton."
"The busy kind. It's not life-threatening, just annoying. For you. I've got more important things to do here."
"Then let's get on with it. Clock is ticking."
"What else? I'm not a *brain* doctor. Look on the bright side -- you've got a whole new life now. Use it wisely."
"What, you want me to do blood work for you again, tell you just how bad things really are *across the board*? You want another rundown of everything collapsing inside your body?"
"With all the damage you've been dealing yourself with drugs and alcohol, I'm not surprised."
"Yes, positive thinking is a well-known cure-all. My suggestion is to exercise a lot."
"Yes, there's no end to the misfortunes fate has seen fit to rain upon me."
"Yes. Probably in more ways than one."
"You must have me confused for a close personal friend... I am not. I am a medical professional -- with a constant *idiot* emergency on my hands."
"You want the real, honest-to-god truth? Stop drinking, eat magnesium and vitamin D. Our station is not a retirement home. We don't have the funds to deal with *rock stars* past their prime."
"Yup."
